subject: kolkrabbi
title: Subscription-limit continuity: durable pause, token-free lift probe, and mid-turn auto chain-walk across the user's own equivalents (vendor CLIs, gateway, local endpoints)
one_why: No other subject treats 'one of my four plans hit its cap mid-turn' as a first-class recoverable state: the pause persists in the session, a monitor confirms the lift without spending a token (key-status//models/sign-in checks), and auto mode resumes the pending turn on the next equivalent model - the whole failure mode every multi-subscription user hits is engineered around.

subject: kolkrabbi
title: Three-stage sacrificial compaction (tool-results, then collapsed tool traffic, then summary) that stops at the first stage that fits, triggers only on provider-measured prompt tokens, and is undoable via on-disk archive
one_why: Nuance vs seeded id and codex's tiers: the trigger refuses to fire on an unknown or guessed window (compacting on a guess is worse than a readable provider error), it compacts to half the window rather than to the threshold so the next turn does not re-trigger, and tool results are emptied-not-removed to keep call/result pairing provider-valid - plus RestoreCompaction and an archive path make the one lossy operation reversible.

subject: kolkrabbi
title: Doom-loop guard keyed on identical call AND identical result bytes, with a 9-slot cycle window for alternating-call loops, checked before the repeat executes
one_why: Best-reasoned loop detector in the corpus: success is the wrong discriminator (a test failing differently is progress; an identical successful read x3 is waste), fixed threshold that does NOT scale with effort (a bigger budget shouldn't buy longer stalls), and the window catches the remove-and-recreate alternation that resets consecutive counters - their own observed failure. crush remains the anchor but this refines the rule.

subject: kolkrabbi
title: Floor-first ordering: hardline refusals bind every tier including full-auto, then user-written rules, then the tier; subagents convert Ask to Deny; 'always' answers land in the visible session rule list, never silently persisted
one_why: The ordering is the design and it is documented as such: 'full-auto stops asking, it does not stop refusing'. The subagent Ask->Deny rule (a child that cannot ask must not inherit ask-scoped autonomy, and the refusal names the switch that legitimately widens it) is directly portable to any subject with background agents; kept-rules going into /permissions rather than a private cache closes the 'always that outlived its session' hole.

subject: kolkrabbi
title: Escape tests that only pass if the KERNEL refused: refusedByTheOS distinguishes kolk declining (exit -1), the pre-exec child guard (exit 125), and a real sandbox denial (platform refusal phrase)
one_why: The corpus's sandbox claims mostly die at exactly this ambiguity: a test that asserts 'the command did not happen' passes when the wrapper merely skipped it. Kolkrabbi's fixture plants a credential canary and demands the platform's own refusal string, so pre-enforcer commits fail red; fail-closed everywhere else (Landlock ABI<4 network-deny refused not approximated, !darwin&&!linux refuses all sandboxed commands). Test-honesty pattern every jail claim in this study should adopt.

subject: kolkrabbi
title: mockagent: shell-script fake vendor CLIs that record received signals, proving the SIGINT->SIGTERM->SIGKILL spawn ladder rung-by-rung against deliberately uncooperative children
one_why: Signal escalation is untestable with stock tools - you need a child that traps SIGINT and one that exits on it, and an exit code cannot distinguish which rung fired, so the fake logs the signals it received. Scripts not binaries on purpose (no toolchain, no GOCACHE, seconds not minutes); the reasoning why SIGKILL-first invalidates a vendor session (destroys the result frame) is written down next to the proof.

subject: kolkrabbi
title: Architecture as data with a no-escape-hatch ratchet: layer import rules, engine-purity ('the engine touches no OS'), naming, plus ~14 named CI gates; knownViolations fails on both add AND un-removed-fix
evidence: internal/arch/layers.go:1-32; Makefile:58-74; .github/workflows/ci.yml (arch, purity, buildtags, budgets, surface, spec, plan-check, workflow-pin-check)
one_why: Stronger than ouroboros's size ratchet and cline's docs: the ratchet list cannot rot because the test also fails when a listed violation has been fixed but not removed, violations are edited as reviewed data not suppress comments, and 'purity' means the core loop is OS-free by CI, not by convention - which is what makes the 0-god-file, 3-surface tree (tui/cli/serve) actually stay that way at bus factor 1.

subject: kolkrabbi
title: Hardline command floor is word-list matching (sudo/mkfs/dd-of-dev/rm-rf-root/curl|sh/force-push) - bypassable by indirection, but explicitly labeled 'not a perimeter' with the jail named as the real control
one_why: Convergence entry for the corpus regex-denylist cluster (6 prior): the mechanism itself is the usual weak one ($(HOME) indirection, absolute-path dd, env splitting all slip past), but unlike claii-class subjects the code and docs state the ceiling in the same breath and route real enforcement to tiers + seatbelt/Landlock - the honest-framing half is the transferable artifact, and it pairs with aeon-9's permission-policy nuance.

subject: kolkrabbi
title: Effort as a cross-cutting routing dial: one setting simultaneously selects model tier, per-turn tool-round budget, shell timeout, and orchestration task width
one_why: Everyone has a thinking-budget dial (ultrathink); nobody else's scales the harness instead of the model: low = flash-class model, 4 rounds, 30s shells, 1 task; ultra = frontier tier, 80 rounds, 900s, 8 concurrent tasks - coherent resource posture per level with alias migration tested, and the pairing with per-slot model config makes cost/latency/blast-radius a single user-facing decision.

subject: kolkrabbi
title: KolkBench: pre-registered benchmark methodology that holds the model constant to measure the harness, with the failed local-8B pilot published as its own finding
one_why: The evals-in-CI gap is the corpus's known ceiling and everyone scores models; this is the only pre-registered attempt to score agent loops against each other with model/repo/prompt pinned - and the pilot writeup states the validity condition ('when every harness scores zero the score is measuring the model'). No comparative run yet, so it scores as method + honesty, not as results.
